statements.claim: The war at Kurukshetra was over and the Pandavas had won it; Krishna was preparing to return to Dwaraka when Uttara cried out.
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.7-8 (Sanskrit): gantuṃ kṛtamatir brahman dvārakāṃ ratham āsthitaḥ — Krishna resolved to go to Dwaraka and mounted his chariot; pack index places the scene as Krishna departing Hastinapura after the war.

statements.claim: Uttara cried 'Protect me, protect me, great yogin, Lord of gods, master of the world! May this blazing iron-tipped arrow burn me, but let my embryo not fall.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt of SB 1.8: 'Uttara cries: Protect me, protect me, great yogin, Lord of gods, master of the world! May this blazing iron-tipped arrow burn me, but let my embryo not fall.'

statements.claim: Uttara was the daughter of King Virata.
statements.evidence: Pack: 'the womb of Virata's daughter.'

statements.claim: Drona's son Ashvatthama had loosed his weapon so that the Pandavas would be left without an heir, targeting the unborn child.
statements.evidence: Pack: 'the Lord... understood that Drona's son's weapon was aimed to leave the Pandavas without heir'; index: 'the unborn Parikshit.'

statements.claim: The weapon was the Brahmashira, unerring and beyond any counter.
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.14 (Sanskrit in pack): 'yadyapyastraṃ brahmaśirastvamoghaṃ cāpratikriyam' — the brahmashira weapon is unerring (amogha) and not to be counteracted (apratikriya).

statements.claim: By his own maya Krishna entered the womb and shielded the child with the Sudarshana disc, extinguishing the unerring Brahmashira.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'Krishna enters her womb by his yoga-maya and shields the unborn Parikshit with the Sudarshana disc, extinguishing the unerring Brahmashira.' Verse excerpt states the womb was covered by his maya to preserve the Kuru line — summary is the pack's intended reading.

statements.claim: 'Do not be astonished, for all wonders have their home in him.'
statements.evidence: SB 1.8.15: 'mā maṃsthā hyetadāścaryaṃ sarvāścaryamaye ñcyute' — do not think this a wonder, for all wonders abide in Acyuta.

statements.claim: The child was born whole and would be called Parikshit, heir of the Kuru line; Uttara kept her own life and the child's.
statements.evidence: Pack title/index: 'Krishna Shields Parikshit in Uttara's Womb'; maya covered the womb 'to preserve the Kuru line.'

statements.claim: 'The war had won them a kingdom and cost them nearly everything else; the next generation of their house had been cut down in the terrible days after the fighting.'
statements.evidence: Background framing consistent with the pack's 'leave the Pandavas without heir' and the SB context of Ashvatthama's night attack; the specific killings are not detailed in the pack verses.

notes: All factual claims supported by SB 1.8.7-15 pack. The Sudarshana-disc shielding follows the pack summary (verses themselves say maya covered the womb); no contradiction. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Hearing that Krishna and his warriors were coming and thinking they would attack, King Shrigala of Karavira rode out of the city to strike first.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v1: 'Being informed of their arrival and thinking that they would attack the city, king Shrigāla, terrible in battle and endued with the prowess of Indra, issued (out of the city).'

statements.claim: Shrigala's chariot had golden axles, was packed with weapons and inexhaustible quivers, was drawn by swift horses, coursed like Garuda, shone like the sun and resembled the car of Indra.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v2-6: car 'filled with weapons... filled with inexhaustible arrows and quivers... drawn by quick-coursing horses, embellished with strong golden axles, coursing like Garuda... effulgent like the sun and resembling the car of Indra.'

statements.claim: The earth was said to sink beneath Shrigala's weight, and he approached Krishna like an insect approaching a flame.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v7, v11: 'Shrigāla approached Krishna like an insect approaching a flame'; 'Stricken with fear at his shouts... the Earth sank under his weight.'

statements.claim: Krishna was not pained and sat at ease as Shrigala approached.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v12-13: 'Vāsudeva was not pained'; 'Shrigāla ran towards him like unto clouds ranging towards a mountain... Vāsudeva... seated at ease.'

statements.claim: Shrigala taunted Krishna about his work among the weak kings on Mount Gomanta and the useless Kshatriyas, declared himself emperor of the world, and offered a fair single combat: 'If thou art slain... I shall be the only Vāsudeva in the world. And if I am slain thou shalt be the only one.'
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v17-22, quoted nearly verbatim in the pack passage.

statements.claim: Krishna replied 'Strike me as you wish' and held up his discus.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v23: 'Hearing those words of Shrigala and saying Strike me as you wish the forgiving Mādhava held up his discus.'

statements.claim: The encounter resembled two infuriated elephants meeting in a forest.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v14-15: 'a dreadful encounter between them like that of two infuriated elephants in a forest.'

statements.claim: Shrigala lost his senses in anger, loosed a net of arrows and hurled maces and flaming weapons at Krishna, who stood motionless like a mountain.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v24-26: net of arrows, 'showered on Krishna mace and various other weapons... covered with flames of fire Krishna stood there motionless like a mountain.'

statements.claim: Krishna hurled the discus at Shrigala's breast; his heart pierced, the king fell bleeding like a cleft mountain.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v27-29: 'holding up his discus he hurled it at Shrigala's breast... Shrigala too, having his heart pierced by the discus... fell down, bleeding like a cleft mountain.'

statements.claim: The soldiers fled or wept in the city; Krishna said 'Do not fear! Do not fear!' to the people; the subjects, ministers and queens with their sons wept over the fallen king.
statements.evidence: HV 1.100 v30-40: soldiers fled, some entered the city weeping, some performed rites; Krishna declared safety and said 'Do not fear! Do not fear!'; subjects/ministers/queens with sons wept.

notes: Story tracks HV 1.100 (Dutt) almost scene-for-scene, including the dialogue verbatim. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: The routed Asuras broke and ran; Nikumbha shamed them: 'You promised to avenge the destruction of your kinsmen... What will your wives say? Fie on you! Fie on you!'
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v1-6: Nikumbha, filled with anger, asked why they broke their promise to avenge their kinsmen and cried 'What will your wives say? Oh fie on you! fie on you!'

statements.claim: Filled with shame, the Asuras returned with double vigour and re-engaged the Yadavas at the sacrificial ground of the martial festival; Dhananjaya, Bhima, Nakula, Sahadeva and Yudhishthira destroyed those who came; sky-borne foes were slain by Indra's son and Pravara.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v7-9: Asuras 'returned with double vigour'; the five Pandava brothers 'destroyed all who went to that sacrificial ground where took place the martial festivity'; 'Those, who rose up into the sky, were slain by Indra's son and the foremost of the twice-born Pravara.'

statements.claim: The field ran with a river of blood thick as a rainy-season stream.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v10-12: 'there flew a river of blood like a stream filled with water in the rainy season.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha struck Pravara down with his iron club (parigha); Indra's son Jayanta caught and embraced his comrade, then ran back at the Asura; wounded by shafts, Nikumbha resolved to fight Krishna, who had killed his kinsmen, rather than exhaust himself on Indra's son.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v13-19: Nikumbha struck Pravara with his Parigha; Indra's son held him up, embraced him, and ran at the Asura; 'the great Asura thought: I shall fight... with my enemy Krishna who has killed my kinsmen. Why do I make myself exhausted by fightlng with Indra's son.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha vanished and reappeared where Krishna stood; Indra on Airavata had come with the gods to watch, and celestial trumpets sounded for Jayanta's victories.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v20-23: Nikumbha 'disappeared from that place and went where the highly powerful Krishna was'; 'Seated on his Airāvata... Vāsava, had come there with the gods to witness the battle'; 'celestial trumpets were struck at the command of the king of gods.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha set up a leonine shout and attacked Krishna, Arjuna, Bhima, Yudhishthira, the brothers, the Yadava chiefs and the kings, and by his illusory powers none of those masters of weapons could see him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v24-28: Nikumbha with a leonine shout attacked Garuda, Baladeva, Satyaka, Nārāyana, Arjuna, Bhima, Yudhisthira, Sahadeva, Nakula, Vasudeva, Shāmva and Pradyumna; 'none among those heroes, masters of all sorts of weapons, could see him.'

statements.claim: Krishna meditated on Vilwodakeshwara, the lord of goblins, and by that lord's power everyone could see Nikumbha standing like the summit of Kailasa.
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v28-30: 'Hrishikesha (Krishna) meditated upon Vilwodakeshwara, the lord of goblins'; all 'could at once see Nikumbha... stationed before them like the summit of the Kailāsa.'

statements.claim: Arjuna had strung Gandiva and his shafts struck Nikumbha's body but shattered and fell broken; he asked Krishna, 'My arrows, resembling thunderbolts, pierce even the mountains. But why are they useless here?'
statements.evidence: HV 1.232 v31-33: 'Pārtha had set string to his Gāndiva bow... they fell down on earth shattered and broken'; Dhananjaya asked 'My arrows... pierce even the mountains. But why are they useless here?'

statements.claim: Nikumbha fled to the cave of Shatpura, stronghold of his kin; Krishna followed; commanded by an invisible voice to use the discus and saluting Mahadeva, Krishna discharged the Sudarshana, which sundered Nikumbha's head with its earrings from his body.
statements.evidence: Pack title/summary: Krishna 'follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana'; excerpt: 'saluting Mahādeva he discharged his discus Sudarshana... sundered Nikumbha's head adorned with most beautiful ear-rings.'

notes: Every beat maps to HV 1.232 passage (v1-33) + pack excerpt and title. Krishna's reply 'O son of Kunti, hear' begins exactly where the printed passage truncates; the cave/voice/discus ending is covered by the pack title and excerpt. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: While the Yadavas were absorbed in their sports and Dwaraka lay unguarded, the wicked, unapproachable Danava Nikumbha, enemy of the gods and bent on his own destruction, stole away Bhanumati, the beautiful daughter of Bhanu.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v1-2: 'While the virtuous Yadavas were thus sporting the highly wicked and unapproachable Dānava, Nikumbha, the enemy of the gods, desirous of bringing on his self-destruction, finding a loop-hole, stole away the beautiful daughter of Bhānu by name Bhānumati.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha was avenging an old enmity: Pradyumna had earlier carried off Prabhavati, daughter of Nikumbha's brother Vajranabha, and Vajranabha had been killed.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v3-4: 'formerly, the daughter of his brother Vajranābhā, by name Prabhāvati, had been taken away by Pradyumna and Vajranābha had been killed. Remembering this former enmity... he... stole away Bhānumati.'

statements.claim: Bhanumati was taken from the garden attached to her father Bhanu's women's quarters — a garden that was unapproachable but stood without guards because the Yadavas were busy with their sports.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v4-5: 'played upon the women of the Yādavas'; 'Although the garden, attached to the female appartment of Bhānu, was unapproachable, still at that time there were no guards for the Yadavas were busy with their sports.'

statements.claim: As the weeping maiden was carried away a great tumult arose in the women's quarters.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v6: 'while that weeping maiden was being carried away there arose all on a sudden a great tumult in the female appartment.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva and Ahuka rushed out filled with wrath and, finding no offender, went in their sport dress to Krishna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v7-8: 'the heroes, Vasudeva and Ahuka issued out, filled with wrath. And not seeing the offender before them, they, in that dress, went where the highly powerful Krishna was.'

statements.claim: Krishna, hearing of the insult, rode Garuda (enemy of serpents) with Arjuna, commanded Pradyumna (whose banner bore the Makara) to follow in his chariot, and bade Garuda fly.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v9-10: 'Janārddana... rode, together with Pārtha, Garuda the enemy of the serpents. Having commanded the hero having the emblem of a Makara on his flag to follow him on his car he asked Kashyapa's son Garuda to proceed.'

statements.claim: 'The whole city of Dwaraka at leisure, its palaces open, its gardens unwatched... was exactly what Nikumbha had been waiting for.'
statements.evidence: Atmosphere consistent with v1-5 (Yadavas sporting, no guards); motive framing not stated verbatim in pack.

statements.claim: Nikumbha was a master of illusion who knew a hundred ways to vanish, so finding him would take all the speed of Garuda, all the arrows of Arjuna and all the cunning of Pradyumna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v4, v12: Nikumbha 'proficient in illusions'; Pradyumna 'the foremost of those conversant with illusions.'

notes: Faithful to HV 1.237 v1-11 and the pack summary (ocean sport, unguarded garden, revenge motive). Story ends where the pursuit begins; the overtaking/rescue is the next story's content. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Before Nikumbha could reach the city of Vajra, Krishna and Arjuna overtook him on the way.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v11: 'before Nikumbha, unconquerable in battle, could reach the city of Vajra, Pārtha and Krishna... overtook him in the way.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna, foremost of those conversant with illusions, divided himself into three portions.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v12: 'the highly powerful Pradyumna, the foremost of those conversant with illusions, divided himself into three portions.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha, smiling, fought all three with heavy clubs while holding the weeping maiden in his left hand.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v13: 'Nikumbha, like unto an immortal, smilingly fought with them all with heavy clubs. Holding the maiden Bhānumati by his left hand... repeatedly hurled the club with his right hand.'

statements.claim: Krishna, Pradyumna and Arjuna could not strike ruthlessly lest they wound the maiden; they sighed with compassion for her and, following the rules of their art, struck the demon with cane-like arrows without touching the maiden.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v14-18: none 'could strike him ruthlessly lest they might wound the maiden'; they 'began to sigh piteously out of their excessive compassion'; 'Pārtha, Kāma and Krishna did not strike the maiden but wounded the Danavas with their cane-like arrows.'

statements.claim: Arjuna shot as a man strikes a serpent coiled round a camel, leaving the beast untouched.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v17: 'As when a serpent gets round a camel... so Pārtha, the foremost of archers, began to strike the Daitya with his arrows.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha vanished with the maiden by illusion and went on assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture; Arjuna assailed him with arrows piercing his vitals.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v19-21: Nikumbha 'so disappeared with the maiden... nobody could know it'; 'he, however, went on assuming the semblance of a yellow vulture'; Dhananjaya 'assailed him again with cane-like arrows piercing his very vitals.'

statements.claim: Pursued across the whole earth of seven insular continents, Nikumbha dropped down on the bank of the river Chela Ganga on the summit of Mount Gokarna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v22-23: 'that great Asura... travelled all over the earth consisting of seven insular continents and dropped down with the maiden at last on the bank of the river Chela Gangā flowing on the summit of the mount Gokarna.'

statements.claim: No god, Asura or great ascetic could cross that mountain, protected by the energy of Mahadeva; Pradyumna found the weak point and snatched Bhanumati away.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v24-25: 'None amongst the gods, Asuras or great ascetics could cross that mountain protected by the energy of Mahadeva. Finding this weak point of Nikumbha... Pradyumna... got hold of the maiden Bhānumati.'

statements.claim: Krishna and Arjuna assailed Nikumbha with arrows; he fled from the northern range of Gokarna to the southern range, pursued by the two Krishnas on Garuda.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v25-26: 'Krishna, and Arjuna began to assail the Asura greatly with arrows. Then leaving the northern range of the mount Gokarna, Nikumbha fled to the southern range. Both the Krishnas however, riding on Garuda, pursued him.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha entered Shatpura, the abode of his kinsmen; Krishna and Arjuna spent the night at the mouth of the cave; Pradyumna, with Krishna's permission, took Bhanumati back to Dwaraka and returned; the three heroes then occupied the entrance of Shatpura waiting for Nikumbha.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v27-30: Nikumbha 'entered into Shatpura, the abode of his kinsmen'; the two heroes spent the night at the cave mouth; 'With Krishna's permission the heroic son of Rukshmini... took... daughter to the city of Dwārakā... and returned'; Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna 'waited there.'

notes: Scene-for-scene match with HV 1.237 v11-30 including the serpent-camel simile and cane-like arrows detail. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Bhanumati, daughter of Bhanu, had been snatched from the women's garden by the demon Nikumbha while the city was absorbed in its sports; Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna chased him across the earth and brought her safely home; the demon was shut up in his mountain stronghold.
statements.evidence: HV 1.237 v1-30 (pack): abduction from the unguarded garden, pursuit, rescue at Gokarna, Nikumbha confined in Shatpura; recap is consistent with the same chapter.

statements.claim: The sage Narada came to Dwaraka and supplied the explanation that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a curse.
statements.evidence: Pack title/summary: 'Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages.'

statements.claim: Long before, the girl had excited the anger of Durvasa, the foremost of sages, who imprecated a curse that she must fall into the hands of an enemy.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.237, Narada's speech): 'this your daughter excited the anger of the foremost of Munis Durvāsā who... imprecated a curse on her saying:— she must fall into the hands of an enemy.'

statements.claim: The sages had softened the curse: Bhanumati would fall into an enemy's hands as the words demanded, but that is where its working ended — she would be taken, and she would be restored.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'a Durvasa curse softened by the sages'; chapter narrative has the abduction followed by rescue and restoration, matching the limited working.

statements.claim: The abduction by Nikumbha, the long chase and the rescue at Mount Gokarna were the curse doing exactly what it had been permitted to do, and no more.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the pack summary's softened-curse reading and the HV 1.237 events (abduction → pursuit → rescue at Gokarna → return).

statements.claim: Bhanu gave his daughter in marriage to Sahadeva, the youngest of the five Pandava brothers, in Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: '...do you now confer her on Sahadeva.' Sahadeva is the youngest Pandava (standard corpus fact); wedding location Dwaraka follows from the Dwaraka setting of the chapter.

statements.claim: 'The demon had believed he was avenging an old wrong and choosing his own hour. Perhaps he was. But beneath his malice had run an older current, set in motion years before by a sage's anger.'
statements.evidence: Interpretive commentary that synthesizes the pack's two strands (Nikumbha's revenge motive v3-4 and the Durvasa curse excerpt); no separate factual assertion.

notes: Supported by pack summary + excerpt (HV 1.237 Narada passage: Durvasa curse, 'confer her on Sahadeva'). No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Krishna was hidden under a growing mound of rocks where his chariot had stood — buried by torrents of rocks.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'torrents of rocks falling upon me covered me up... covered along with my horses and charioteer and flagstaffs, with crags on all sides, I disappeared from sight altogether.'

statements.claim: Salwa came to war from his flying city Saubha, a fortress of costly metal that could move through the sky wherever he willed, and devastated Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'that car of precious metals capable of going anywhere at will'; Daruka: 'he... devastated Dwaraka'; story's pack title/locations: Saubha (aerial city).

statements.claim: Krishna had gone out to meet Salwa in single combat in the air; the fight began as a duel of archery against the enemies who crowded the aerial city.
statements.evidence: Framing for the excerpted battle (MBh 3.22 begins mid-duel with Krishna cutting off heads 'from off that car of costly metals'); the specific 'single combat in the air' staging is not within the pack passage itself but is consistent with the Salwa episode.

statements.claim: Krishna loosed arrows shaped like serpents, capable of great height and intense energy, cutting down the enemies of the celestials.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'I began to discharge from the Sharanga many well-looking arrows of the forms of snakes, capable of going at a great height and possessing intense energy.'

statements.claim: The car vanished through illusion; Krishna was filled with wonder; Danavas of frightful visages and hair set up a loud howl; Krishna slew them with the weapon that strikes at sound, answering yells from all ten directions with mantra-charged arrows until the invisible hosts were silent.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: car 'had vanished, through illusion... I was then filled with wonder'; 'host of Danvas... of frightful visages and hair, set up a loud howl'; shafts 'capable of striking at the perception of sound alone'; yells from 'all the ten quarters above and across' answered with 'arrows of diverse forms, and celestial weapons inspired with mantras.'

statements.claim: The car of precious metals reappeared at Pragjyotisha and the Danavas drowned Krishna in a mighty shower of rocks, so that he grew like an ant-hill with summits and peaks.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'that car of precious metals... bewildering my eyes, reappeared at Pragjyotisha'; 'the destroying Danavas of fierce forms suddenly drowned me with a mighty shower of rocks... I began to grow like an ant-hill (with its summits and peaks).'

statements.claim: Krishna's Vrishni army, struck with panic, fled in all directions; heaven, firmament and earth were filled with cries of 'Oh!' and 'Alas!'; friends wept while enemies rejoiced.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'those foremost of heroes of the Vrishni race who were of my army were, struck with panic, and all on a sudden began to fly in all directions'; 'the heaven, the firmament, and the earth were filled with exclamation of Oh! and Alas!'; 'my friends... began to weep and wail... delight filled the hearts of the enemies.'

statements.claim: Wielding the thunderbolt, Indra's favourite weapon capable of riving stones, Krishna destroyed the entire mass of crags; his horses stood trembling, almost at the point of death, and his friends rejoiced as at the sun dispersing clouds.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'wielding the thunderbolt, that favourite (weapon) of Indra, capable of riving stones, I destroyed that entire mass of crags'; 'my steeds, afflicted with the weight of the stones and almost on the point of death began to tremble'; friends 'rejoiced... even as men rejoice on seeing the sun rise in the sky, dispersing the clouds.'

statements.claim: Charioteer Daruka urged Krishna: 'Behold Salwa... Do not disregard him... Slay Salwa — do not let him live... this one has devastated Dwaraka.'
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22, Daruka's speech quoted near-verbatim in the pack passage: 'behold Salwa the owner of the car of precious metals sitting (yonder)... Slay Salwa... do not let him live... he... devastated Dwaraka.'

statements.claim: Krishna fixed his blazing weapon of fire to the bowstring, bade Daruka stay a moment, and hurled the discus Sudarshana — sharp-edged as a razor, unstained, reducing Yakshas, Rakshasas and Danavas to ashes — which rose like a second sun, went through the town of Saubha as a saw divides a tall tree, and cut the flying city in twain.
statements.evidence: MBh 3.22: 'saying unto Daruka, Stay a moment I fixed on my bow-string my favourite weapon of fire... the great powerful discus Sudarsana which reduceth to ashes in battle Yakshas and Rakshasas and Danavas... sharp-edged like the razor, and without stain'; 'rising into the sky, it seemed like a second sun... the discus went right through it, even as a saw divideth a tall tree. And cut in twain by the energy of the Sudarsana.'

notes: Near-verbatim rendering of MBh 3.22 (Ganguli). The 'single combat in the air' opening line is connective framing outside the excerpted passage (flagged RCN); everything else directly supported. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Krishna held the reins of Arjuna's chariot at Kurukshetra, having come as a charioteer, not a fighter.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 excerpt: 'Vasudeva's son, abandoning (the reins of) the steeds, jumped down from the car'; the army trembled 'in the very presence of Vasudeva and the high-souled Partha' — Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer is the fixed frame of the battle narrative.

statements.claim: After the forenoon had passed and the Pandavas had won the first part of the day, Devavrata (Bhishma, son of Santanu) was carried by his fleetest steeds into the mass of his enemies, and a dreadful engagement followed.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'After the forenoon of that day... had passed away... and after the high-souled Pandavas had won the victory, thy sire Devavrata... rushed carried by the fleetest steeds, towards the army of the Pandavas... commenced a dreadful battle, making the hair stand on end.'

statements.claim: The battle sounds — twang of bows like splitting hills, cries of 'Stay! Here I stand!' and 'Turn back!', fall of golden armour and diadems like stones on stony ground — and a river of blood miry with the bodies of men, horses and elephants, with vultures and jackals at its edges.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: uproar 'resembling that of splitting hills'; words 'Stay--Here I stand... Turn back' heard everywhere; falling coats of gold mail 'resembled the sound of falling stones on a stony ground'; 'dreadful river of blood... miry with flesh and blood... Flowing from the bodies of steeds, men, and elephants, and delightful to vultures and jackals.'

statements.claim: Bhishma's bow, drawn into a circle, shot blazing shafts like venomous snakes; not one arrow was futile; he smote the Pandava car-warriors, naming each one beforehand; his lightness of hands made him seem to dance like a circle of fire present everywhere.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'Bhishma... with bow incessantly drawn to a circle, shot shafts of blazing points, resembling snakes of virulent poison'; 'smote the Pandava car-warriors naming each beforehand'; 'displaying his extreme lightness of hands, and dancing (as it were) along the track of his car, he seemed... to be present everywhere like a circle of fire'; 'Not a single shaft of that light-handed warrior was futile.'

statements.claim: The Pandavas and Srinjayas saw Bhishma, though really alone, multiplied a thousand-fold, now east, now west, now north, now south; they could not even look at him and saw only the countless shafts.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'the Pandavas in that battle, along with the Srinjayas, beheld that hero, though really alone, as multiplied a thousand-fold'; 'Having seen him now on the east, the next moment they saw him on the west... on the north... on the south'; 'There was no one amongst the Pandavas capable of even looking at him. What they all saw were only the innumerable shafts.'

statements.claim: Thousands of kings fell upon the enraged Bhishma like flights of senseless insects upon a blazing fire; a single straight shaft despatched a single elephant as a hill is riven by thunderbolt, and one arrow pierced two or three armoured riders standing together.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'kings in thousands came in contact with thy sire... and fell upon that fire represented by the enraged Bhishma like flights of senseless insects'; 'With a single straight shaft... he despatched a single elephant like hill riven by the thunderbolt. Two or three elephant-riders at a time, cased in mail and standing together, thy sire pierced with one shaft.'

statements.claim: Whoever approached Bhishma was seen for a moment and the next moment was seen falling; the vast host of King Yudhishthira gave way in a thousand directions and trembled in the presence of Vasudeva and Partha.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59: 'Whoever approached Bhishma... seen for a moment, was next beheld to fall down on the ground'; 'that vast host of king Yudhishthira the just... gave way in a thousand directions'; 'the vast army began to tremble in the very presence of Vasudeva and the high-souled Partha.'

statements.claim: Krishna abandoned the reins, jumped down from the car whirling the discus Sudarshana — beautiful nave, edge sharp as a razor, effulgent as the sun — and rushed impetuously toward Bhishma like a lion springing upon a prince of elephants blinded with fury.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 excerpt: 'Vasudeva's son, abandoning (the reins of) the steeds, jumped down from the car, whirling with his (right) arm his discus of beautiful nave with edge sharp as a razor, effulgent as the sun... the high-souled Krishna rushed impetuously towards Bhishma... like a lion from desire of slaying upon a prince of elephants blinded with fury.'

statements.claim: The grandsire, who had named every warrior before he shot, had not named this one (Krishna).
statements.evidence: Closing flourish tying v11 (Bhishma named Pandava car-warriors beforehand) to Krishna's unannounced charge; consistent with the excerpt.

notes: MBh 6.59 (Ganguli) rendered almost clause-for-clause, including Bhishma's feats and the closing charge. 0 UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.
